title: Round 2: adversarial counterexample attempts on round-1 candidates
question: For each listed hypothesis, find a counterexample, a boundary case where the statement fails, a hidden assumption, or a flaw in the stated derivation; or record a reproducible failed attempt.
claims: H1: abstract lemma is correct but uses only F(x0)=x0 and f(Fx0)=c f(x0); the claimed application misdescribes pairings: e(.,R) with non-rational R is not Galois-equivariant for c=q (toy k=2 curves: f(pi X)=f(X) != f(X)^p), the r | q^j-1 condition is the embedding-degree definition, and the anomalous map is a group hom on E(F_p) with trivial Frobenius action; 'unification' is vacuous (cyclic Hom counting). Experimental/proof-attempt only.
H2: no violation of M(M+1) for all prime powers q<=150000 (and 400 samples to 1e6), M<=12; proof checked with no gap; provable sharper bound 2*sum phi(m) - M (tight at M=1,2). Survived attack.

H3: count 4^L(L!)^2 correct for exactly-L programs but the 'length <= L' inference has a gap (needs sum_{i<=L}); counting bound is vastly weaker than the trivial 2^{L+1}+1 bound (L>=log2 r -1); L0(2^256)=29 and L0(2^521)=50 reproduced as length lower bounds; per-op bit-cost assumption unjustified, final omega(n log n) holds only in the black-box SLP model.

H4: psi is a homomorphism on E~(Z_p), so consistent lifts Q~=[k]P~ give psi(Q~)=k psi(P~) with probability 1 (statement false under the universal 'arbitrary lifts' reading); for independent uniform lifts (psi(P~),psi(Q~)) is exactly uniform on F_p^2 (exhaustive enumeration on 30 curves), randomized rates match 1/p; p | #E with r != p only possible for p=5 (#E=10) among p>=5.
